chapter: Learning drums and Roy Eldridge's band
title: Roy's embouchure change and his New York trip
summary: Dance and Clarke discuss Roy's range, his tooth trouble, and how his stay in New York made him a local god.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Well, Roy didn't have all that, because when I knew Roy, which was, say, two years later -- I mean when Roy went into the Three Deuces, he explained to me then that he wasn't going to be able to blow anything for some months, because he was switching his embouchure armature so he could get range.
I see.
And he couldn't, he could hit very few notes. He just altered his embouchure armature altogether so he could get at least another octave.
I see.
And that's what he started -- don't you remember, because he didn't have that high range when he -- in the beginning, remember?
No, he used to play -- he used to play Armstrong a lot of Louis's records and things, Louis's solos.
yeah.
And I remember Roy was having trouble with his two front teeth here.
Yeah, maybe that could have actually caused him to figure he should change that embouchure armature, too.
Uh-huh.
Yeah.
Because he had like two snags in the front, you know.
Oh, yeah. Yeah.
But he had been to New York, he had played at Small's Paradise and all that.
You mean all on his own he went to New York?
This was after he had been in New York and he came back home.
For heaven's sake.
And of course everyone thought, well, Roy's the king, you know, he's been to New York, and Small's Paradise, he's played with all the great musicians.
Yeah, the big time.
You know. So he was like our god.
Was Joe blowing too?
Yes, oh, yes. Yes.
But had Joe gone with him or had Roy gone on his own?
No, I think Roy went on his own.
Yeah, I think so too.
Because Joe was around home, you know, writing and --
He was a different temperament.
Yeah, he was. Very quiet, you know.
